To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the high fructose feeding was accompanied by an increase in the activity of fructo kinase and CoASAc-carboylase and a decrease in the concentration of citrate in rat liver, which in turn resulted in an increase in the hepatic fatty acid concentration.
the differential effects of diets high in glucose, fructose or sucrose on hepatic fatty-acid synthesis are related to differences in the hepatic phosphorylation of glucose and fructose.

the differential effects of diets high in glucose and fructose content upon lipogenesis depend upon differences in the hepatic concentrations of glycolytic intermediates, the rate of conversion of glucose and fructose to fatty acids, and the activity for the enzymes of fatty acid synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the mechanism by which a fructose-rich diet increases hepatic lipogenesis.
the effects of high carbohydrate intake on the hepatic concentration and synthesis of fatty acids in rats fed either a chow diet, a glucose diet or a fructose diet.
a better understanding of the mechanism for the regulation of hepatic lipogenesis in rats fed high carbohydrate diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high fructose diet increased the hepatic concentration and activity of the lipogenic enzymes to a greater extent than a diet of similar carbohydrate content but high in glucose.

the increased lipogenesis in the liver of rats fed a high fructose diet is due to an increase in hepatic CoASCo carboxylase activity, which is a consequence of the higher rate of hepatic fructose metabolism to CoA-S-CoA.
fructose is a much stronger lipogenic substrate than glucose in the rat liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fructose feeding increases the rate at which fatty acid is synthesized from carbohydrate by increasing the availability of CoASAc.

the differential effects of glucose and fructose on lipogenesis are a consequence of the greater rate of CoASAC formation from fructose than from glucose and the greater activity of the CoASAc carboylase in fructose-fed rats than in rats fed a chow diet.
the high rate of CoASAccarboxylation is the primary factor responsible for the increased rate of fatty acid synthesis in rat liver fed high glucose or frucose diets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fructose-rich diet is not as bad as a glucose-rich diet, at least in terms of the liver’s response.
the rate of fatty acid synthesis in rat liver depends on the rate of CoASac formation.
the rate at which fructose was metabolized to acetyl-CoA was greater than that for glucose.
